mainTopic: The 'wall' of a pit in the משנה, and the argument between אביי and רבא about digging next to the boundary (מצר)
overview: The גמרא asks why the משנה starts by talking about a neighbor's pit but then says to keep away from his 'wall.' אביי (some say רב יהודה) explains that it means the wall of the neighbor's pit, and the word teaches that a pit's wall is three טפחים thick. This matters when someone sells 'a pit and its walls.' Next, אביי and רבא argue about digging right at the boundary when the neighbor has no pit yet. One version says they argue only about a field not meant for pits. Another version says they argue only about a field meant for pits, and it brings support from the rules about planting trees near a pit. The גמרא then tests both versions against the משנה, and each side defends itself: רבא with 'from the wall of his pit,' and אביי by saying the משנה is about two neighbors digging at the same time. A ברייתא about soft, crumbly rock is brought against אביי but is pushed off as a special case. A new proof about olive waste and manure begins, and it continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why does the משנה switch from 'pit' to 'wall'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה begins with a neighbor's pit but ends by saying to keep away from his wall. It asks why the משנה didn't just say 'from his fellow's pit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה opens by talking about a pit but ends by talking about a wall. It should have said: unless he kept three טפחים away from his fellow's pit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning the wording of the משנה. The משנה starts with one word, 'pit,' and finishes with a different word, 'wall.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says not to dig a pit near a neighbor's pit 'unless he distanced it from the wall of his fellow three טפחים.' Since the case is about pits, it seems the ending should also say 'pit.' The switch to 'wall' looks out of place, so the גמרא wants an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Opens with... and ends with (a pointer to a change in wording)
Let it teach / it should have said

phrases.english: GEMARA
He opens with a pit, and ends with a wall;
phrases.notes: The משנה opens: don't dig a pit near your neighbor's pit. Then it says to keep away from his 'wall.'

phrases.english: let it teach: unless he distanced it
from the pit of his fellow three handbreadths!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה ('wall' instead of 'pit')
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case is about a neighbor's pit, so the ending should match and say 'pit,' not 'wall.'

steps.title: The משנה means the wall of the neighbor's pit
steps.stepSummary: אביי (some say רב יהודה) answers that we should read the משנה as 'from the wall of his pit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was רב יהודה: we learned the משנה as 'from the wall of his pit.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי (or רב יהודה) answers the question. The 'wall' in the משנה is the wall of the neighbor's pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not changing topics. 'Wall' is short for 'the wall of the neighbor's pit.' So you measure the three טפחים from the edge of his pit's wall.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (the statement may belong to a different sage)
We learned (this is how the משנה reads)

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say it was Rav Yehuda:
we learned: "from the wall of his pit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the משנה moved from talking about a pit to talking about some other wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Wall' means the wall of the neighbor's pit, so the משנה stays on the same topic.

steps.title: Then why not just say 'pit'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. If 'wall' means the wall of the pit, the משנה could simply have said 'from his fellow's pit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But even so, let it teach: unless he kept three טפחים away from his fellow's pit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. If the meaning is the pit's wall anyway, why use the extra word 'wall'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We would understand on our own that keeping away from a pit means keeping away from its edge. So the word 'wall' seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what the extra word teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: But let it teach (pressing the same point again)

phrases.english: But let it teach: unless he distanced it
from the pit of his fellow three handbreadths!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיתְנֵי: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִרְחִיק מִבּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading 'from the wall of his pit'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'wall' just means the pit's edge, the plain word 'pit' would have said the same thing. So why mention a wall at all?

steps.title: The wording teaches that a pit's wall is three טפחים
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'wall' teaches a new fact: the wall of a pit is three טפחים thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that the wall of a pit is three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'wall' was chosen on purpose. It teaches us how thick a pit's wall is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture the neighbor's pit near the boundary. Its wall fills the three טפחים between the hole and the boundary. By calling that space 'the wall,' the משנה tells us that a pit's wall is three טפחים thick.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us (a new point hidden in the wording)

phrases.english: This teaches us
that the wall of a pit is three handbreadths;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra wording teaches a new fact
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'wall' teaches that a pit's wall is three טפחים thick.

steps.title: Where this matters: selling a pit and its walls
steps.stepSummary: The fact that a pit's wall is three טפחים matters in buying and selling. A ברייתא says that someone who sells 'a pit and its walls' must give walls three טפחים thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference this makes is for buying and selling, as a ברייתא teaches: one who says to his fellow, 'I am selling you a pit and its walls,' the wall must be three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why it matters to know how thick a pit's wall is. It brings a ברייתא about selling a pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might wonder why we need to know a pit wall's thickness. The answer is buying and selling. If a seller sells 'a pit and its walls,' the buyer gets three טפחים of land around the pit, because that is the size of a 'wall.'

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that comes out of it

steps.whatToRemember: The 'wall' in the משנה is the wall of the neighbor's pit. The משנה uses that word to teach that a pit's wall is three טפחים thick. This matters when someone sells 'a pit and its walls.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a small detail of wording into a practical rule for sales contracts.

phrases.english: The practical difference is for buying and selling,
as it is taught in a baraita:
One who says to his fellow:
"I am selling you a pit and its walls,"
the wall must be three handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical use of the fact taught in step 4
steps.raayaObject: That a pit's wall is three טפחים thick has a real legal effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about someone who sells 'a pit and its walls'

steps.title: אביי and רבא argue about digging next to the boundary
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: someone wants to dig right next to the boundary of his field. אביי says he may, and רבא says he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about one who comes to dig right next to the boundary, אביי says he may, and רבא says he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between אביי and רבא. The question is whether a person may dig or place things right up against the boundary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה dealt with a neighbor who already has a pit. Here the neighbor has no pit there yet. אביי allows digging right at the boundary, since there is nothing to damage now. רבא forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an argument between אמוראים)
He may place it close / he may not place it close

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the case of the משנה. Here the neighbor has no pit at the boundary yet.

phrases.english: It was stated:
one who comes to place something close beside the boundary,
Abaye says: he may place it close,
and Rava says: he may not place it close.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the משנה's distancing rules
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: one may dig or place things right at the boundary. רבא: one may not.

steps.title: Where אביי and רבא actually disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the argument. If the neighbor's field is meant for pits, everyone forbids digging at the boundary. They only argue about a field that is not meant for pits.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a field that is meant for pits, everyone agrees he may not dig right up against it. Where they argue is a field that is not meant for pits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines exactly which case the argument is about. This sets the stage for the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the neighbor's field is the kind where people dig pits, he will likely dig one near the boundary someday. Even אביי agrees you may not dig there and block him. The argument is only about a field where pits are not expected.

keyTerms.meaning: When they disagree / where the argument is

phrases.english: With a field that is designated for pits,
phrases.notes: This is the neighbor's field on the other side of the boundary.

phrases.english: all agree he may not place it close;
when they disagree,
it is with a field that is not designated for pits.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשָׂדֶה הָעֲשׂוּיָה לְבוֹרוֹת דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the argument in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Next to a field meant for pits, no one may dig at the boundary. The argument is only about a field not meant for pits.

steps.title: אביי's reason: the neighbor's field is not meant for pits
steps.stepSummary: אביי allows digging at the boundary because the neighbor's field is not a field where pits are dug.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: He may dig close to the boundary, since the neighbor's field is not meant for pits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אביי's reason for allowing someone to dig right at the edge of his own field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the neighbor's field is not used for pits, there is no pit there that could be harmed. So, for אביי, there is nothing to protect and no reason to keep away from the boundary.

keyTerms.meaning: He may place it close (right up to the boundary)
Meant for pits (a field where people normally dig pits)

phrases.english: Abaye says: He may dig close to the boundary,
since [the neighbor's field] is not meant for pits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in אביי's reasoning in the case narrowed in Step 7: a field not meant for pits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a field not meant for pits, one may dig right at the boundary because no pit there can be harmed.

steps.title: רבא's reason: the neighbor may also change his mind
steps.stepSummary: רבא forbids digging at the boundary, because the neighbor could later decide to dig a pit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: He may not dig close to the boundary, because the neighbor can say to him: 'Just as you changed your mind and dug, I may also change my mind and dig.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's reason for forbidding digging right at the boundary, even though the neighbor's field is not meant for pits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The digger's own field was not meant for pits either, and he still decided to dig. So the neighbor may also decide to dig one day. If the first person dug right at the edge, the neighbor would then have to keep his own pit far away.

keyTerms.meaning: You changed your mind (you made a new decision)

phrases.english: Rava says: He may not dig close to the boundary,
because [the neighbor] can say to him:
Just as you changed your mind and dug,
I too may change my mind and dig.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view to אביי in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not dig at the boundary, because the neighbor keeps his right to dig a pit in the future.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא protects what the neighbor might do in the future, not only what exists right now. This difference is the heart of the whole argument.

steps.title: A second version of where the argument is
steps.stepSummary: Some say the opposite of Step 7: everyone allows digging next to a field not meant for pits, and the argument is only about a field that is meant for pits.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: In a field that is not meant for pits, everyone agrees he may dig close. Where they argue is a field that is meant for pits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the argument. It flips which case everyone agrees on and which case they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 7), everyone forbids digging next to a field meant for pits. In this version, everyone allows digging next to a field not meant for pits. The argument moves to the harder case, a field meant for pits.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (a second version of the same discussion)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In version one, they argue about a field NOT meant for pits. In version two, they argue about a field that IS meant for pits.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
In a field that is not meant for pits,
everyone agrees he may dig close;
where they argue is in a field that is meant for pits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative to the framing given in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Next to a field not meant for pits, everyone permits digging at the boundary. The argument is about a field meant for pits.

steps.title: אביי: allowed even according to the Rabbis about trees
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, אביי permits digging even next to a field meant for pits. He shows this fits even the רבנן who require distancing a tree from a pit, because there the pit already exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: He may dig close, even according to the רבנן who say a tree must be kept twenty-five אמות from a pit. There, when he plants, the pit is already there. But here, when he digs, there is no pit yet.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his view in the second version and explains why the strict ruling of the רבנן about trees does not argue against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן require distance only when the pit already exists at the time of planting. Here the neighbor has no pit yet, only a field that could have one someday. So even the רבנן would let him dig.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view in the משנה)
One must keep at a distance

phrases.english: Abaye says: He may dig close,
even according to the Rabbis, who say:
phrases.notes: This quotes a משנה later in this פרק, on 25b.

phrases.english: One must keep a tree away from a pit
twenty-five cubits.
That is only there, because at the time he plants,
the pit is already there;
but here, at the time he digs,
there is no pit [in the neighbor's field].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אביי's position inside the second version from Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may dig at the boundary even next to a field meant for pits, because no pit exists there yet.

steps.title: רבא: forbidden even according to רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, רבא forbids digging. He says this fits even רבי יוסי, who lets each person plant in his own field, because digging causes damage right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: He may not dig close, even according to רבי יוסי, who says each one may dig or plant in his own field. That is only there, because when he plants, the roots that would harm the pit do not exist yet. But here the neighbor says: 'Every single hoe-strike you make loosens my ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his view in the second version and explains why the lenient ruling of רבי יוסי does not argue against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי is lenient with a tree because the harm, the roots, comes only later. Digging is different: each strike of the hoe weakens the neighbor's soil right now. So the damage is immediate, and even רבי יוסי would forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who is lenient about planting near a pit

steps.whatToRemember: Second version: אביי says it is allowed because there is no pit yet. רבא says it is forbidden because the digging itself loosens the neighbor's soil right away.

phrases.english: And Rava says: He may not dig close,
even according to Rabbi Yosei, who says:
This one digs in his own [field]
and that one plants in his own.
That applies only there,
because at the time he plants,
the roots that would harm the pit are not there yet;
but here, [the neighbor] can say to him:
Every single hoe-strike that you strike
loosens my ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אֵינוֹ סוֹמֵךְ – וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view to אביי's position in Step 11, within the second version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not dig at the boundary next to a field meant for pits, because the digging itself damages the neighbor's soil right away.

steps.title: An inference from the משנה: with no pit, one may dig close
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which forbids digging only next to an existing pit, and concludes that where there is no pit, one may dig close.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: A person may not dig a pit close to his fellow's pit. The reason is that there is a pit there. But if there is no pit, he may dig close.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the wording of our משנה to test the two versions of the argument. This step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only an existing pit, so the גמרא reads it as saying: where there is no pit, digging close is allowed. Now each version must explain which kind of field the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: But if there is not (introduces the opposite case)

phrases.english: We learned [in the Mishnah]:
A person may not dig a pit
close to his fellow's pit.
The reason is that there is a pit;
but if there is no pit, he may dig close.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לֹא יַחְפּוֹר אָדָם בּוֹר סָמוּךְ לְבוֹרוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the two versions to test them against the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Which version of the אביי and רבא argument fits the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'close to his fellow's pit,' which suggests that with no pit, digging close is allowed.

steps.title: The משנה fits the second version
steps.stepSummary: The second version easily explains the משנה as talking about a field not meant for pits, where everyone allows digging close. This hints at a problem for the first version.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to the version that says everyone allows digging close next to a field not meant for pits: our משנה is talking about a field not meant for pits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the second version fits the משנה easily. The word בשלמא signals that the next line will bring a difficulty for the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, everyone agrees about a field not meant for pits, so the משנה's lenient implication can be about that case. In the first version, רבא forbids digging even in that case, so the משנה seems hard to explain for him. That challenge comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one side; a 'but' against the other side usually follows)

phrases.english: It works well according to that version where you said:
phrases.notes: This is the second version, from Step 10.

phrases.english: in a field that is not meant for pits,
everyone agrees he may dig close;
[so] our Mishnah is about a field that is not meant for pits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inference from Step 13 to the second version, as setup for a challenge to the first version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first version (Steps 7 to 9), especially רבא's view that one may not dig even next to a field not meant for pits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that with no pit, digging close is allowed. The second version can place that in a field not meant for pits. The first version has trouble explaining it, and that difficulty is about to be stated.

steps.title: In the first version, the משנה is a problem for רבא
steps.stepSummary: In the first version, the argument is about a field not meant for pits. There the משנה fits אביי but is hard for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the version that says they argue about a field not meant for pits: for אביי it works out fine, but for רבא it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the first version and says the משנה, which allows digging close where there is no pit, seems to go against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the argument is about a field not meant for pits. אביי allows digging close there, and רבא forbids it. The משנה only forbids digging next to an existing pit, which suggests digging close is fine when there is no pit. That matches אביי and clashes with רבא.

phrases.english: But according to that version in which you said:
phrases.notes: This is the first version, from Step 7.

phrases.english: they disagree about a field that is not meant for pits
granted, for Abaye it works out well,
but for Rava it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the hint from Step 14 by stating the problem for the first version openly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies digging close is allowed when there is no pit, but רבא forbids it in a field not meant for pits.

steps.title: רבא answers: the משנה means measuring from the pit's wall
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with the statement of אביי (or רב יהודה) that the משנה is talking about the wall of the pit. So the משנה never allowed digging right at the border.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can say to you: wasn't it said about this משנה, in the name of אביי (some say רב יהודה), 'We learned: from the wall of his pit'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself by pointing to a known statement explaining the משנה as talking about the wall of the pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this reading, the neighbor's pit has a wall three טפחים thick between its hole and the border. So the neighbor who dug first did not dig right at the border; he kept his hole three טפחים away. That means the משנה never allows digging right up against the border, which fits רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned: from the wall of his pit

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not inventing a new idea here. He is quoting a statement already said about the משנה, from Step 2. It is said in the name of אביי, his opponent in this argument, though some say it was רב יהודה.

phrases.english: Rava can say to you:
wasn't it stated about it,
Abaye said, and some say it was Rav Yehuda:
we learned: from the wall of his pit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רָבָא: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה using an accepted statement about it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow digging right next to the border when there is no pit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה measures from the pit's wall, so even it requires keeping away from the border, which fits רבא.

steps.title: Another telling: the same 'wall of his pit' statement
steps.stepSummary: Some people tell this exchange differently. They bring the same statement, 'from the wall of his pit,' but use it to attack אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: and it was stated about the משנה, in the name of אביי (some say רב יהודה), 'We learned: from the wall of his pit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second telling (איכא דאמרי) that quotes the same statement again. This is setting up a new challenge in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as before, but the job is different. Here the statement is not a defense for רבא. It is the starting point of a challenge. It shows that the neighbor who dug first also kept his hole three טפחים, the width of his pit's wall, away from the border.

keyTerms.meaning: there are those who say (another version)

phrases.english: There are those who say:
and it was stated about it,
Abaye said, and some say it was Rav Yehuda:
we learned: from the wall of his pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the statement from Step 16, now as the basis of a challenge instead of an answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה measures from the wall of the pit, so the pit must be kept away from the border.

steps.title: The first version fits this reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: In the first version, everyone agrees you may not dig close to a field meant for pits. So the משנה can be explained as talking about such a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the version that says that in a field meant for pits everyone agrees one may not dig close, our משנה is talking about a field meant for pits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the first version has no problem with this reading. This is setting up the problem for the second version in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the field meant for pits is a case where everyone agrees: no digging close. If the משנה is about that kind of field, it fits both אביי and רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: a field meant for digging pits

phrases.english: Granted, according to that version in which you said:
phrases.notes: This is the first version, from Step 7.

phrases.english: in a field meant for pits
everyone agrees he may not dig close,
our Mishnah is about a field meant for pits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reading from Step 17 to the first version and finds that it fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: Sets up the challenge to the second version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first version has a case of full agreement where the משנה can fit. The next step shows the second version lacks this.

steps.title: In the second version, the משנה is a problem for אביי
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the argument is about a field meant for pits. There the משנה, which requires keeping the pit's wall away from the border, fits רבא but is hard for אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the version that says they argue about a field meant for pits: for רבא it works out fine, but for אביי it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי in the second version, because the משנה now seems to forbid what he allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, the field meant for pits is where אביי and רבא argue. Here אביי allows digging close and רבא forbids it. If the משנה shows that even the first digger kept his hole three טפחים from the border, it agrees with רבא and goes against אביי.
steps.whatToRemember: Each version of the argument causes trouble for one side. The first version seems to go against רבא, and he answers with 'מכותל בורו שנינו'. In the איכא דאמרי telling, that same statement is turned into a challenge against אביי in the second version.

phrases.english: But according to that version in which you said:
phrases.notes: Now it means the second version, from Step 10.

phrases.english: they disagree about a field meant for pits
granted, for Rava it works out well,
but for Abaye it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 18 shows the first version fits, this step shows the second version runs into trouble for אביי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה, read as 'from the wall of his pit', requires keeping away from the border in a field meant for pits, but אביי allows digging close there.

steps.title: אביי explains the משנה as both neighbors digging at once
steps.stepSummary: אביי can say the משנה is talking about two neighbors who come to dig their pits at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can tell you: our משנה is talking about a case where both neighbors came to dig at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against אביי from the last step. It shows how אביי reads the משנה so that it does not argue with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that if your neighbor has no pit yet, you may dig right up to the border. The משנה, read as 'from the wall of his pit,' seems to show that the first digger also kept his hole three טפחים away. אביי answers that the משנה is only about both neighbors digging together, so each one must leave room. When only one is digging, he may still dig at the border.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you: a way of giving someone's answer for him

phrases.english: Abaye can say to you:
Our Mishnah is where they came to dig at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 19 against אביי in the second version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה is limited to two neighbors digging at the same time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to require distance in every case, against אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only requires distance when both neighbors dig together. A lone digger may dig at the border.

steps.title: A teaching about soft rock seems to go against אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that with soft rock, each neighbor keeps three טפחים away and plasters the pit. This seems to mean that even the first digger must keep away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: with rock that crumbles in your hands, this one digs his pit from here and that one digs his pit from there. This one keeps three טפחים away and plasters with lime, and that one keeps three טפחים away and plasters with lime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack אביי. The ברייתא seems to describe one neighbor digging first and still having to keep his distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says "this one digs from here, and that one digs from there." That sounds like one after the other, not both at once. If even the first digger must keep three טפחים away, then אביי's answer that only digging together needs distance does not seem to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
Rock so soft that it crumbles in your hands

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rock that crumbles in the hands,
this one digs his pit from here,
and that one digs his pit from there;

phrases.aramaic: זֶה מַרְחִיק שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים וְסָד בְּסִיד,
phrases.english: this one keeps three handbreadths away and plasters with lime,

phrases.aramaic: וָזֶה מַרְחִיק שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים וְסָד בְּסִיד!
phrases.english: and that one keeps three handbreadths away and plasters with lime!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 20 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that you only need distance when both neighbors dig together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא seems to describe digging one after the other, yet the first digger still keeps three טפחים away.

steps.title: Soft rock is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back the proof: rock that crumbles in your hands is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rock that crumbles in the hands is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof against אביי. It says the ברייתא is about a special kind of ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft rock crumbles easily, so a pit near the border could damage the neighbor's ground. That is why distance is needed there even for the first digger. In normal ground, אביי's rule still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different: a special case that does not teach the general rule

phrases.english: Rock that crumbles in the hands is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 21 against אביי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ברייתא as a proof about normal ground.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about soft rock, which has its own reason to require distance.

steps.title: Why did anyone bring this proof at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why the questioner brought a ברייתא that clearly speaks about a special kind of rock.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who asked it, why did he ask it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question: the ברייתא plainly says "soft rock," so why did anyone think it proves something about normal ground? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer "soft rock is different" seems so obvious that the challenge looks weak from the start. The גמרא wants to understand what the questioner was thinking.

keyTerms.meaning: And the one who raised it

phrases.english: And the one who asked it, why did he ask it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the challenge in step 21, now that step 22 rejected it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the questioner thought a ברייתא about soft rock could teach about all ground.

steps.title: The questioner thought soft rock was mentioned to limit the distance
steps.stepSummary: The questioner thought the ברייתא covers all ground. Soft rock was named only to teach that even there, three טפחים is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for the case of soft rock. You might have thought that since it crumbles in the hands, it needs even more space. So it teaches us that three טפחים is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the questioner was thinking. He read the ברייתא as a rule for all ground, with soft rock as the hardest example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the questioner's reading, soft rock is not why distance is needed. It was named to stop us from thinking it needs more than three טפחים. So, for him, the three טפחים rule applies to all ground, which would go against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him: it had to be said
You might have thought to say

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the גמרא's final answer about soft rock. It only explains how the questioner read the ברייתא. The rejection in step 22 still stands.

phrases.english: Rock that crumbles in the hands was needed for him,
phrases.notes: He means the תנא had a reason to mention soft rock, even though the rule covers all ground.

phrases.english: it could enter your mind to say:
since it crumbles in the hands,
it should also need more space;
it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: Three טפחים is enough even for soft rock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The questioner thought soft rock was mentioned only to teach that it does not need more than three טפחים. So he read the rule as applying to all ground.

steps.title: A new source begins: keeping olive waste and manure away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts bringing a משנה that lists things one must keep away from a neighbor's wall: olive waste, manure, and more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one must keep away olive waste, and manure, and
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof by starting to quote a משנה. The quote continues past this point, so the full argument comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists harmful things a person must keep away from his neighbor's wall. The גמרא will use it to test the argument between אביי and רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: One must keep at a distance
Solid waste left after pressing olives

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הַגֶּפֶת, וְאֶת הַזֶּבֶל, וְאֶת
phrases.english: One must keep away the olive waste, and the manure, and

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the soft-rock proof was rejected, the גמרא begins a new source to test אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument between אביי and רבא about digging near the border (continues in the next part).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated; the quote of the משנה is still being set up.
